description: RColSim is an R river-system model for reservoir operations in the Columbia River Basin. Its contributors publish scripts to examine flood protection, irrigation demand, environmental flows and hydropower objectives at dam and system scales. The workflow prepares weekly streamflow and demand inputs, reads rule curves and flow targets, runs operations and calculates performance measures. Coverage is the Columbia River Basin in the Pacific Northwest; the scenario determines the simulated period. The README describes 45 dams, while the JORS abstract states 46, so the count remains unresolved in this draft. GitHub provides the source, documentation and example workflow under MIT, permitting free reuse. Base R supplies most operations, with xts needed by input-preparation scripts. A limitation is its dependence on basin-specific operating assumptions and suitable streamflow and demand inputs. It supports comparison of climate stressors and operating policies. Related record model-pownet addresses power-system operations that can depend on hydropower availability, without a verified direct interface. No scenario inputs were downloaded and no performance claim was reproduced.
inputs: Reservoir rule curves and flow targets
name: RColSim
notes: G5 G5-0033. The repository README describes 45 dams, whereas the JORS abstract describes 46. The draft preserves this discrepancy rather than choosing a count. The earlier data-archive draft for dam re-operation is an output dataset, not the RColSim model. Regional scope is the Columbia River Basin. No simulation was run.
outputs: Flood, irrigation, environmental-flow and hydropower performance metrics
